# Output Format Reference

Templates for all files generated by project-onboard.
Read this file BEFORE generating any output.

## CLAUDE.md Template

CLAUDE.md is a decision tree for the AI agent, NOT documentation for humans.
Keep it under 150 lines. Use task-based routing.

```markdown
<!-- generated by project-onboard -->
# Project: {name}
{one-liner description from README or interview}

## Tech Stack
{auto-detected: framework, language, ORM, DB, etc.}

## Commands
- Dev: `{dev command}`
- Build: `{build command}`
- Test: `{test command}`
- Lint: `{lint command}`
{add more from package.json scripts or Makefile as relevant}

## ⚡ Context Available — DO NOT explore
Context files are pre-generated in .claude/context/.
Read ONLY the files relevant to your current task.
DO NOT run find/ls/tree to explore. Trust these files.
Last updated: {date} | Run /onboard-update to refresh

## When to read what

BEFORE modifying or creating any API endpoint:
  → read .claude/context/features/api-endpoints.md
  → read .claude/context/features/db-schema.md

BEFORE modifying or creating any page or component:
  → read .claude/context/features/pages-views.md
  → read .claude/context/features/_feature-map.md

BEFORE modifying database schema or migrations:
  → read .claude/context/features/db-schema.md
  → read .claude/context/features/_feature-map.md (check impact)

BEFORE writing or modifying tests:
  → read .claude/context/testing-strategy.md

WHEN you need to understand how a feature works end-to-end:
  → read .claude/context/features/_feature-map.md

WHEN you need to understand project architecture or patterns:
  → read .claude/context/architecture.md
  → read .claude/context/conventions.md

WHEN you encounter domain terms you don't understand:
  → read .claude/context/business.md

WHEN deploying or working with CI/CD:
  → read .claude/context/workflow.md

WHEN using a framework API you're unsure about:
  → read .claude/context/stack-docs/

## Warnings
{top 3-5 critical warnings inline}
- Full list: read .claude/context/warnings.md

## Testing
{one-line strategy summary, e.g., "TDD, Vitest, target 80%"}
- Details: read .claude/context/testing-strategy.md
<!-- end generated by project-onboard -->
```

### Rules for CLAUDE.md

1. NEVER exceed 150 lines
2. NEVER just list files — always use BEFORE/WHEN routing
3. NEVER include information that belongs in context files
4. ALWAYS preserve existing user-written content when merging
5. Mark generated sections with HTML comments
6. Include the "DO NOT explore" instruction — this is critical

## Context File Templates

Every context file follows this structure:

```markdown
# {Title}
> Read this file WHEN {trigger condition}.

## How to use
{1-2 lines explaining what the agent should do with this info}

## Content
{structured, concise, actionable content}
```

### architecture.md

```markdown
# Architecture
> Read this file WHEN you need to understand project structure or patterns.

## How to use
Use this as your map. Do NOT run find/ls/tree — this file is your source of truth.

## Directory Structure
{tree output of key directories, 2 levels deep, annotated}

src/
  app/           → Next.js App Router pages + API routes ({N} routes)
  components/    → Shared React components ({N} files)
  lib/           → Utilities, DB client, helpers
  services/      → Business logic layer
  types/         → TypeScript type definitions
prisma/          → Database schema + migrations

## Key Architecture Decisions
- {pattern}: {why and how}
- {pattern}: {why and how}

## Key Files
- {path} → {what it does, when you'd need to read it}
```

### conventions.md

```markdown
# Conventions
> Read this file WHEN writing new code or reviewing patterns.

## How to use
Follow these conventions for all new code. Check existing code matches.

## Code Style
{from eslint/biome/prettier config}

## Naming
- Files: {pattern, e.g., kebab-case.ts}
- Components: {pattern, e.g., PascalCase}
- Functions: {pattern}
- Database: {pattern}

## Patterns
- {pattern name}: {brief description}
  Example: {one-line code example}

## Import Order
{if detectable from config or existing code}
```

### workflow.md

```markdown
# Workflow
> Read this file WHEN deploying, working with CI/CD, or branching.

## How to use
Follow this process for all code changes.

## Branch Strategy
{detected from git branches or interview}

## CI/CD Pipeline
{from GitHub Actions / GitLab CI config}
- Trigger: {when}
- Steps: {what runs}

## Deploy
- Target: {Vercel/AWS/Docker/etc.}
- Command: {how}
- Environments: {staging, production, etc.}

## Git Hooks
{from .husky/ or pre-commit config}
```

### business.md

```markdown
# Business Context
> Read this file WHEN you encounter domain terms or need project context.

## How to use
Reference these terms when reading or writing code that uses domain language.

## What This Project Does
{from README + interview}

## Domain Terms
| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| {term} | {definition} |

## Users
{who uses this and how}
```

### testing-strategy.md

```markdown
# Testing Strategy
> Read this file BEFORE writing or modifying any tests.

## How to use
Follow this strategy for all test-related work.

## Approach
{TDD / test-after / none — from interview}

## Frameworks
- Unit/Integration: {vitest/jest/etc.}
- E2E: {playwright/cypress/none}

## Coverage
- Target: {X%}
- Current: ~{Y%} ({N} test files found)

## What to Test
- Unit: {what}
- Integration: {what}
- E2E: {what}

## Rules
{from interview, e.g., "write test before code", "every PR needs tests"}
```

### warnings.md

```markdown
# Warnings
> Read this file WHEN planning any significant change.

## How to use
Check this list before modifying files. Ask the user if unsure.

## Do Not Modify Without Asking
- {path}: {reason}

## Common Pitfalls
- {pitfall}: {how to avoid}

## Breaking Change Risk
- {area}: {why it's risky}
```

## .claudeignore Template

Generate if not exists:

```
node_modules/
.next/
dist/
build/
coverage/
__pycache__/
.venv/
*.lock
*.min.js
*.map
public/assets/
.git/
```
